instagram_reel.script:
If the weather is warm, I’m reaching for rosé. And if it’s an Ontario rosé I can actually buy at the LCBO? Even better.

This one is the Hidden Bench Locust Lane Rosé 2025, and it’s a really lovely bottle from Beamsville Bench in Niagara. It’s pale salmon in the glass, and the nose gives you strawberry, white flowers, and a little flinty edge.

On the palate, it’s dry and fresh, with cherry, candied lime, nectarine, and pink peppercorn. So pretty, but not precious.

It’s made mostly from Pinot Noir, with a touch of Viognier, and at $26.95, this is one to keep in mind for patio season or your next dinner with friends.

tiktok.script:
Okay, if you want a rosé that feels like a real treat but is still easy to find, keep an eye out for Hidden Bench Locust Lane Rosé 2025.

It’s from Beamsville Bench in Niagara, and it’s got that pretty pale salmon colour, plus notes of strawberry, white flowers, cherry, candied lime, nectarine, and a little pink peppercorn.

What I like is that it’s dry, fresh, and just very well put together. Not fussy. Just really good.

It’s $26.95 at the LCBO, and honestly, that’s the kind of bottle I’d be happy to bring to a patio hang or dinner with friends.

linkedin.post:
When a wine from Ontario earns a spot on the LCBO shelf, it deserves a little attention.

Hidden Bench’s Locust Lane Rosé 2025 is a strong example of the quality coming out of Niagara’s Beamsville Bench. Hidden Bench has built its reputation on small-lot, estate-grown wines, and this rosé reflects that same thoughtful approach.

The wine is made primarily from Pinot Noir, with a touch of Viognier, and comes in at $26.95 at the LCBO. It’s a timely reminder that Ontario rosé can be both accessible and serious in the best way: dry, fresh, and distinctly place-driven.

For trade, retailers, and brand partners, this is the kind of bottle that helps tell the bigger story of what Niagara is capable of. Consumers are looking for wines with character, local relevance, and real value — and this checks those boxes.

It’s a good bottle for patio season, dinner with friends, or simply for anyone looking to explore Ontario wine a little more intentionally.
